dossier.public_summary: The dip depth swings wildly from near zero to more than a percent between sectors and even between individual transits, and odd and even dips differ by about 10% at high significance – both classic signs of an eclipsing binary at twice the 1.48-day period, not a planet. The signal is centered on the target star, but the variable depth and large phase-curve swing favor a stellar companion or blended variability over a 5.9 Earth-radius planet.
